Answer: D
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates diffuse bronchiectasis (ring shadows and tram-tracking) combined with ground-glass opacities, which, in the context of recurrent lower tract infections, is most characteristic of atypical cystic fibrosis. While other conditions cause bronchiectasis, the specific combination of diffuse cystic changes and parenchymal opacities strongly points to CF over PCD or ABPA.
